prompt.context_jp: 相原家のダイニングには、久しぶりに家族全員の顔____揃っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家族全員の顔____揃っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits this opening line.

feedback.correct_en: This is the chapter's opening scene-setting sentence. が marks the newly introduced information — the fact that everyone's faces were gathered — as a fresh observation to the reader.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 家族全員の顔 as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit a scene-opening description. を is wrong because 揃う is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: As for the family, they were gathered. (topic already known)

prompt.context_jp: 湯気とは裏腹に、母・美登里だけ____硬い表情のまま箸を置いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母・美登里だけ____硬い表情のまま箸を置いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the contrast here?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts Midori alone against the warm atmosphere — everyone else is relaxed, but her alone (だけは) stays stiff. The contrastive は is required after だけ here.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would just identify her, losing the contrast with the rest of the family. を doesn't fit this subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけは笑わなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 「それは お母さん____結婚式の招待状 無視したから」
prompt.prompt_jp: お母さん____結婚式の招待状 無視したから
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this accusation?

feedback.correct_en: Mei is identifying who is responsible — 'it's because YOU (Mom) ignored it'. が picks out the agent in this cause clause and places the focus on her as the one who did it.
feedback.incorrect_en: お母さんは would make Mom the general topic, weakening the pointed accusation. に doesn't fit the agent role here.

contrast_examples.jp: お母さんが無視したから。
contrast_examples.en: Because Mom (was the one who) ignored it.

contrast_examples.jp: お母さんは無視したよ。
contrast_examples.en: As for Mom, she ignored it.

prompt.context_jp: 「無視するって決めたの____私だし」
prompt.prompt_jp: 無視するって決めたの____私だし
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft-like statement.

feedback.correct_en: Mom is owning the decision: 'the one who decided to ignore it, (that) is me.' The nominalized clause 決めたの is set up as the topic, with 私だ as the predicate identifying who.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 決めたの into new-info subject of some other predicate, which doesn't match the 'X は Y だ' identification pattern here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who decided is me.

prompt.context_jp: 張り詰めた口論も、ナギサ____次の皿を運んでくる気配で、ふっと勢いを失った。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサ____次の皿を運んでくる気配で、ふっと勢いを失った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Nagisa inside this relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 気配, the subject takes が: 'the sign that Nagisa was bringing the next dish.' は cannot normally mark subjects inside relative clauses.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the embedded-clause structure. で here would wrongly cast ナギサ as a means or location.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来る音が聞こえた。
contrast_examples.en: I heard the sound of him coming.

contrast_examples.jp: *彼は来る音… (ungrammatical as relative clause subject)

prompt.context_jp: 娘の家で見知らぬ中年男が包丁を握っている──その事実を、彼女____まだ完全には呑み込めていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女____まだ完全には呑み込めていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits before the predicate here?

feedback.correct_en: Midori is already the established topic of the paragraph. 彼女は carries that topic forward and lets the focus fall on 'hasn't fully taken it in'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼女が would reintroduce her as new information, which clashes with the flow. を is already used on その事実 earlier.

contrast_examples.en: SHE is the one who doesn't know. (identifies who)

prompt.context_jp: 「私____すべて習得するのに 3年かかりました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私____すべて習得するのに 3年かかりました
prompt.prompt_en: Nagisa is answering a question about himself. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Nagisa shifts the topic to himself ('as for me') to describe his personal case, contrasting implicitly with other staff. は is the standard choice for this kind of self-topicalization.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would sound like he is identifying himself as 'the one who' did it, which is odd when simply reporting his own timeline.

contrast_examples.en: It took me three years. (my case)
I'm the one who took three years. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサ____余計な相槌を返さずに、問われた分だけを淡々と口にした。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサ____余計な相槌を返さずに…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best marks Nagisa in this descriptive sentence?

feedback.correct_en: Nagisa has already been introduced as the housekeeper in this scene. The narrator is describing his characteristic behavior, so は marks him as the known topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Nagisa as newly spotted information, but he's been central throughout the dinner scene.

contrast_examples.en: HE was the one who spoke calmly.

prompt.context_jp: 若いアシスタントの努力が語られると、美登里の眉間からわずかに力____抜けた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 美登里の眉間からわずかに力____抜けた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence reports a newly observed change — tension dropping from her brow. が introduces 力 as the new element entering the scene with 抜ける.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 力 as a given topic, which doesn't match a sudden observation. を is wrong because 抜ける is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: Tension drained from her shoulders. (spontaneous event)

prompt.context_jp: 事実だけを積み上げていく話しぶり____、かえって信頼を呼ぶ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事実だけを積み上げていく話しぶり____、かえって信頼を呼ぶ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this narrator comment?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is making a fresh, somewhat surprising observation: 'this very manner of speaking is what inspires trust.' が highlights 話しぶり as the (unexpected) source of the effect.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the aha-moment feel and just treat the speech style as a familiar topic. で would turn it into a means, which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: その正直さが信頼を呼ぶ。
その正直さは信頼を呼ぶものだ。
contrast_examples.en: That honesty is the kind of thing that inspires trust. (more generic)

prompt.context_jp: 母の質問____途切れる気配はなく、メイの肩からは緊張がなかなか抜けなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母の質問____途切れる気配はなく…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the subject inside this relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: 母の質問 is the subject of 途切れる inside a relative clause modifying 気配. Subjects of relative clauses take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally cannot appear inside a relative clause like this. を is wrong because 途切れる is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: 普段から寡黙な茂____、こういう肝心な場面で言葉を呑み込みがちだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 普段から寡黙な茂____、こういう肝心な場面で言葉を呑み込みがちだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits here?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is characterizing Shige's habitual tendency. は sets him up as the topic for a general description ('tends to swallow his words').
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a one-time new-information report, not fitting the habitual 〜がちだった. も would wrongly imply 'Shige too'.

prompt.context_jp: 唐突な流れに、美登里____目を丸くしたまま動きを止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 美登里____目を丸くしたまま動きを止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Midori is the established topic of the scene. は continues her as topic and the sentence reports what she did (froze up).
feedback.incorrect_en: 美登里が would reintroduce her as new info, which doesn't fit — she's been central throughout the dinner.

contrast_examples.en: It was Mother who stopped moving.

prompt.context_jp: 母親という肩書きの奥にいる、一人の女の声____、そこにはあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一人の女の声____、そこにはあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this lyrical observation?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence reveals something new: behind the label 'mother,' there was a woman's voice. ある with existential discovery takes が to mark the newly introduced entity.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the voice as a known topic, undoing the moment of discovery.

contrast_examples.jp: そこには別の声があった。
その声はそこにあった。
contrast_examples.en: As for that voice, it was there. (already known)

prompt.context_jp: 娘の下手な変装など、母親に____初めから通用していなかったのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母親に____初めから通用していなかったのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits after 母親に?

feedback.correct_en: The は on にはcontrasts 母親 with others (the disguise fooled other viewers, but not Mom). It also marks the topic 'as for Mom'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot directly follow に. も would imply 'Mom too didn't see through it', the opposite of the intended meaning.

contrast_examples.en: It doesn't get through to him (specifically).
It doesn't get through to him either.

prompt.context_jp: どこか同じ女親として、他人の娘の頑張りに手を合わせるような気配____ある。
prompt.prompt_jp: …ような気配____ある。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with ある here?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is pointing out that a particular atmosphere newly exists in this moment. Existential ある with a freshly observed subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気配はある would sound like contrasting with its absence elsewhere, not a fresh observation. を is wrong because ある is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: 自分の育て方____、そんなふうに娘を追い詰めていたとは、想像もしていなかったのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の育て方____、そんなふうに娘を追い詰めていたとは…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the subject of the embedded clause?

feedback.correct_en: The subject is embedded inside a that-clause ending in 〜とは. Embedded subjects normally take が: 'that her own parenting was cornering her daughter'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to make 育て方 the main topic, but this clause is a complement of 想像もしていなかった. を is wrong for this subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 自分の言葉が娘を傷つけたとは知らなかった。
contrast_examples.en: I didn't know that my own words had hurt my daughter.

contrast_examples.jp: 自分の言葉は娘を傷つける。
contrast_examples.en: My words (as topic) hurt my daughter.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサの心尽くしの料理から立ちのぼる湯気とは裏腹に、母・美登里だけは____表情のまま箸を置いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母・美登里だけは____表情のまま箸を置いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word best describes Midori's expression in this tense moment?

feedback.correct_en: 硬い表情 ('stiff expression') is the standard collocation for a tense, guarded face — exactly the mood contrasting with the warm steam of the dishes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 明るい表情 or 優しい表情 would contradict the whole 裏腹に (opposite of) framing — Midori is specifically NOT relaxed here.

contrast_examples.en: She didn't let her stiff expression soften.

prompt.context_jp: 三年前に家を出たきり消息の途絶えた末娘・唯の話題が、今夜もまた____とうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 唯の話題が、今夜もまた____とうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'the topic was about to be ___ again'?

feedback.correct_en: 蒸し返す is the fixed expression for digging up an old, unresolved topic again — perfect for the recurring argument about Yui.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ち上げる means 'lift up / praise'. 片付ける would mean 'settle / finish', the opposite of what's happening.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサは余計な相槌を返さずに、問われた分だけを____口にした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 問われた分だけを____口にした。
prompt.prompt_en: Which adverb fits Nagisa's quiet, measured way of answering?

feedback.correct_en: 淡々と captures Nagisa's neutral, understated delivery — just the facts, nothing embellished.
feedback.incorrect_en: ぺらぺら implies chatty, almost flippant talking. きっぱり suggests a firm refusal/declaration, which doesn't match a calm answer.

prompt.context_jp: 疑いをぶつけるつもりで始めた会話が、いつのまにか賞賛に近い色を____いる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 賞賛に近い色を____いる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 色を to mean 'take on a tone/shade of'?

feedback.correct_en: 色を帯びる is the set collocation for '(something) takes on a tone/shade of ~'. Here the conversation gradually takes on a color of admiration.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持つ and 作る don't collocate idiomatically with 色 in this abstract sense.

contrast_examples.en: Take on a tone of anxiety.

prompt.context_jp: 母は身を乗り出し、忘れかけていた記憶の糸を____。
prompt.prompt_jp: 忘れかけていた記憶の糸を____。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb idiomatically goes with 糸を to mean 'trace back memories'?

feedback.correct_en: 糸をたぐる (literally 'pull in a thread') is the standard metaphor for pulling at threads of memory one after another.
feedback.incorrect_en: 糸を結ぶ means to tie a thread; 糸を切る means to cut it — neither matches tracing memories back.

contrast_examples.en: Pull at the threads of memory.
Tie a thread of fate (connect people).

prompt.context_jp: 「2人とも いつまでも ____ってばっかりだったからでしょ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 2人とも いつまでも ____ってばっかりだったからでしょ
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'being stubborn' here?

feedback.correct_en: 意地を張る means to be stubborn / refuse to back down out of pride — exactly what Mom is calling out about her two daughters.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気張る means 'to exert oneself'. 胸を張る means 'to be proud / stand tall' — neither matches the standoff between the sisters.

contrast_examples.jp: 意地を張って謝らない。

prompt.context_jp: 「ハァ… ____ 母は強い」
prompt.prompt_jp: ____ 母は強い
prompt.prompt_en: Which word describes Midori as a tough opponent?

feedback.correct_en: 手ごわい means 'formidable / hard to handle' — fitting Mei's exasperation at how tough her mom is as an interrogator.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手堅い means 'reliable, steady' (not threatening). 手軽い isn't a standard word (手軽 means 'easy / simple').

prompt.context_jp: 「メイと唯が 私が作ったハンバーグに 調味料 ____たりして 自分たちの好きな味付けにして 楽しんでた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 調味料を____たりして自分たちの好きな味付けにして楽しんでた
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'adding seasoning'?

feedback.correct_en: 調味料を足す means 'to add more seasoning' — exactly what the sisters did to customize their mom's hamburger.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引く ('subtract') doesn't fit — you can't 'unseason' a finished dish. 混ぜる ('mix') would be odd without an object to mix with.

prompt.context_jp: 「ここからだよ ここから____ね 今こそ タイミングと勢い」
prompt.prompt_jp: ここから____ね
prompt.prompt_en: Which onomatopoeic adverb means 'crisply / decisively'?

feedback.correct_en: ビシッと means 'sharply / decisively / with resolve' — Mei is urging Dad to speak up crisply and not fumble.
feedback.incorrect_en: のんびり ('leisurely') and ぼんやり ('vaguely') are the opposite of what Mei wants from her hesitant father.

prompt.context_jp: メイが『1等賞取れなくてお母さんをがっかりさせちゃうと思ったから』と言い、母が返す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Midori's gentle response?

choices.text: そんなことで がっかりしないわよ
そんなことで がっかりしなかったわよ
そんなことが がっかりしないわよ

feedback.correct_en: The present-habitual 〜しないわよ expresses Mom's general stance ('I wouldn't get disappointed over something like that'). It's warm and reassuring.
feedback.incorrect_en: The past form narrows it to one specific moment and sounds stiff. そんなことが is ungrammatical here — そんなことで (means/reason) is required.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなことで怒らないよ。
contrast_examples.en: I wouldn't get mad over something like that.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなことで怒ったよ。
contrast_examples.en: I got mad over something like that. (odd here)

prompt.context_jp: 変装したまま泣きそうな唯が、懐かしのハンバーグを食べて漏らすセリフ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Yui's quiet, emotional line?

choices.text: もう一生 食べらんないと思ってた
もう一生 食べられないと思っていました
もう一生 食べれるとは思いませんでした

feedback.correct_en: 食べらんない is the casual contraction of 食べられない. The casual register plus ~と思ってた fits Yui's private, stifled sob — she's not addressing anyone formally.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite ~ました form would clash with the intimate, breaking emotional moment. Option (c) is awkwardly phrased and also too formal.

contrast_examples.jp: もう会えないと思ってた。
contrast_examples.en: I thought I'd never see you again. (intimate)

contrast_examples.jp: もうお会いできないと思っておりました。
contrast_examples.en: I thought I would be unable to meet you again. (very formal)

prompt.context_jp: 穴の開いたセーターを「直せる？」と聞かれたナギサの返答。
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply best captures Nagisa's understated, professional confidence?

choices.text: 家政夫ですから、できるかもしれません
家政夫だから、直したいです

feedback.correct_en: The clipped 家政夫なんで (= 'because I'm a housekeeper') lands as a confident, slightly playful 'of course' — exactly Nagisa's deadpan charm.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) weakens the confidence with かもしれません. (c) replaces skill confidence with personal desire (直したい), which misses the humor.

contrast_examples.jp: プロなので、できるかもしれません。
contrast_examples.en: I'm a pro, so I might be able to. (undercuts the confidence)

prompt.context_jp: 高級肉のお返しを辞退しかけたナギサが、受け取る代わりに提案するセリフ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for Nagisa's polite workaround?

choices.text: ここで一緒に食べさせてもらえると 助かります
ここで一緒に食べさせてあげると 助かります
ここで一緒に食べさせると 助かります

feedback.correct_en: 〜させてもらえると助かります is the humble, grateful phrasing: 'if you'd let me eat together with you, it would help me'. It fits Nagisa's polite register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜させてあげる reverses the direction (he'd be doing Mei a favor). 〜させると removes the benefactive and sounds blunt and off.

contrast_examples.jp: お手伝いさせてもらえると助かります。
contrast_examples.en: It would help me if you'd let me assist.

contrast_examples.jp: お手伝いさせてあげます。

prompt.context_jp: 「いつから気づいてた？」と聞かれた母の返答。
prompt.prompt_en: Which variant sounds most natural as Midori's answer?

choices.text: お料理のメニューを見た時から 何となく
お料理のメニューが見た時から 何となく
お料理のメニューを見た時から 何となしに

feedback.correct_en: メニューを見た時から uses を correctly with 見る, and 何となく is the standard adverb for 'somehow / vaguely'. The whole line flows naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) wrongly uses が with 見る. (c) 何となしに exists but sounds literary/stiff — unnatural in this warm family moment.

contrast_examples.jp: 何となしに感じていた。
